text: Are eggs good or bad for cholesterol?
Eggs do contain dietary cholesterol.
It's found in the yolk.
But it isn't the same as the cholesterol in your blood.
For most people, the cholesterol in food
only has a small effect on blood cholesterol.
This means you can enjoy eggs every day
as part of a healthy, balanced diet.

If you have a condition
called familial hypercholesterolaemia,
you may need to be careful about foods
that contain dietary cholesterol
including eggs.
Foods high in saturated fat
like fatty meats, butter, and pastries

are much more likely to raise blood
cholesterol than eggs.
Cutting down on saturated fat

is one of the best ways
to keep your cholesterol healthy
so eggs cooked without butter
like poached or boiled
are the healthier choice.
